summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and obesity, was admitted for chest pressure and worsening shortness of breath. He had been recently discharged with a similar presentation and was found to have decompensated heart failure, with elevated BNP, pulmonary edema on imaging, and bilateral edema. He also exhibited episodes of symptomatic bradycardia and tachycardia on telemetry, leading to cardiology consultation and subsequent implantation of a biventricular pacemaker with ICD. He was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and had his beta-blocker changed to metoprolol tartrate for cost reasons. His diabetes was managed with insulin as metformin was held due to worsening renal function. He improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms and stabilization of vital signs, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged for device monitoring, lab work, and evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea.
